dedupe_keys.name: fabio food and agriculture biomass input output database 1986 2013

description: FABIO is a set of global multi-regional physical supply-use and input-output tables for agriculture and forestry. The Zenodo record says it covers 191 countries plus rest of world, 118 processes and 125 raw and processed agricultural and food commodities for 1986 to 2013, built mostly from FAOSTAT, IEA, EIA and UN Comtrade/BACI, with R code and auxiliary data on GitHub and documentation at fabio.fineprint.global. Components are compressed R (.rds) files: the inter-commodity matrix Z in tonnes (about 24,000 rows and columns), final demand Y, output X, environmental extensions E and Leontief inverses by year in mass and value, plus a classification workbook. Version 1.1 was published on 25 September 2020 by Martin Bruckner and Nikolas Kuschnig (Vienna University of Economics and Business), with 66 files totalling about 8.8 GB, under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Caveats: the non-commercial share-alike licence limits reuse, the series ends in 2013, and physical flows rest on FAO balances. For simulation it gives commodity-by-country supply chains for food and biomass, to trace how crop failures or trade shocks propagate through processing and trade to final demand. Related catalogue records include the Eora2 global supply chain database and the virtual water flows dataset.
